question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? When Emily Brontë's novel Wuthering Heights came out in 1847, her name was nowhere to be seen on the book's cover. The reason is that Brontë had opted ______ a pen name: Ellis Bell.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The verb 'opted' takes the infinitive 'to use' to complete the sentence correctly.

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? An office of the International Criminal Police Organization (Interpol) is located in the city of Bern, Switzerland. Yet you won't find Interpol agents pursuing international criminals through Bern. Although Interpol can assist with investigations, only Swiss authorities ______ allowed to carry out arrests there.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The present tense 'are' matches the ongoing, general fact and the plural subject 'authorities.'

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? Laura Grieneisen is a biologist based at the University of ______ conducts research on primates.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: A period and 'She' correctly separate the two independent clauses.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition? A painter's palette—the surface where the artist lays out and blends paints—can offer valuable insight into that painter's creative process. In her 2024 book The Artist's Palette, Alexandra Loske examines the palettes of 50 different painters spanning 500 years. ______ Loske uncovers clues about the methods and habits of artists such as Kerry James Marshall, Artemisia Gentileschi, and Vincent van Gogh.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: 'In doing so' shows that examining the palettes is the very act that reveals the clues.

question: The student wants to emphasize a difference between Beaux and Artschwager. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal? While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes: The Carnegie Prize is an international art competition run by the Carnegie Museum of Art in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. In 1899, US painter Cecilia Beaux earned a Carnegie Prize gold medal for her painting Mother and Daughter. In 1995, US sculptor Richard Artschwager won a Carnegie Prize gold medal for his sculpture Table Prepared in the Presence of Enemies.
option a: Both Beaux and Artschwager won Carnegie Prize gold medals for their artworks.
option b: Beaux won a Carnegie Prize gold medal in 1899 for the painting Mother and Daughter.
option c: Carnegie Prize gold medals have been awarded to both painters and sculptors.
option d: Beaux won a Carnegie Prize gold medal for a painting, while Artschwager won for a sculpture.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Only this choice contrasts Beaux's painting with Artschwager's sculpture, emphasizing a difference.

question: The student wants to compare the length of time Maria Younghans and Catherine A. Moore worked as lighthouse keepers. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal? While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes: Lighthouses emit essential light signals that help ships and other vessels find their way at night. Prior to automation, lighthouses were operated by lighthouse keepers. Maria Younghans served as the keeper of Biloxi Light in Mississippi, holding the post for fifty-one years (1867-1918). Catherine A. Moore served as the keeper of Black Rock Harbor Light in Connecticut, holding the post for sixty-one years (1817-1878).
option a: Before automation, lighthouse keepers like Maria Younghans, who served for fifty-one years, and Catherine A. Moore were crucial to ensuring safe navigation for watercraft.
option b: Maria Younghans worked as a lighthouse keeper for fifty-one years, but Catherine A. Moore did so for even longer: sixty-one years.
option c: Maria Younghans and Catherine A. Moore were both lighthouse keepers at a time when such a person was needed to operate a lighthouse.
option d: From 1867 to 1918, the nighttime waters of Mississippi were more navigable thanks to lighthouse keepers Maria Younghans and Catherine A. Moore.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Only this choice directly compares the two keepers' lengths of service, fifty-one versus sixty-one years.

question: The student wants to emphasize the combined deadweight tonnage of Greece's merchant ships in 2021. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal? While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes: A merchant ship is any vessel hired to transport cargo or passengers. The amount a ship can carry is known as its deadweight tonnage (DWT). In 2021, a total of 1,236 merchant ships were registered in Greece, and together these ships had a DWT of 64.9 million tons.
option a: There were a total of 1,236 merchant ships—ships hired to carry cargo or passengers—registered in Greece in 2021.
option b: Combined, Greece's merchant ships had a deadweight tonnage of 64.9 million tons in 2021.
option c: In 2021, Greece had 1,236 merchant ships hired to carry cargo or passengers.
option d: The carrying capacity of a merchant ship is also known as deadweight tonnage.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Only this choice states the combined 64.9-million-ton deadweight tonnage the student wants to emphasize.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase? In a 2020 experiment, Kai Ruggeri and his colleagues gave participants from Norway, Belgium, and seventeen additional countries a set of questions that were ______ those used in a landmark 1979 study. By posing the very same questions the earlier study had used, Ruggeri and his team sought to replicate that study's results.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: 'Identical to' fits the follow-up statement that the team used the very same questions.

question: As used in the text, what does the word "produce" most nearly mean? The following text is from Oscar Wilde's 1893 play Lady Windermere's Fan. MRS. ERLYNNE: I am going to live abroad again. The English climate doesn't suit me. My—heart is affected here, and that I don't like. I prefer living in the south. London is too full of fogs and—and serious people, Lord Windermere. Whether the fogs produce the serious people or whether the serious people produce the fogs, I don't know, but the whole thing rather gets on my nerves.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: In context, 'produce' means to cause or bring about one thing from another.

question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined portion in the text as a whole? Research by Mohamed Alburaki, Maria Bouga, and their colleagues indicates that, on the whole, honey bee populations in the US show low genetic diversity. Analyzing a large sample of honey bee specimens gathered from most US states, the researchers identified only three maternal evolutionary lineages within the populations: the North Mediterranean lineage, the West Mediterranean lineage, and the African lineage. Among the specimens from Oregon, they found that 100% descended from the North Mediterranean lineage—a finding in keeping with that for the lineage in many of the other states studied.
option a: It summarizes the central conclusions of the study that is discussed in the text.
option b: It expands on the claim made earlier in the sentence by providing specific data.
option c: It acknowledges that the results of the study discussed in the text are not entirely consistent with the researchers' hypothesis.
option d: It indicates that a result described earlier in the sentence reflects a widespread trend.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The underlined clause shows that Oregon's result matches a pattern seen across many other states.

question: Based on the texts, the author of Text 1 and the author of Text 2 would most likely agree on which point? Text 1: For thousands of years, O'odham farmers in the Sonoran desert of the southwestern US and northern Mexico have grown organ pipe fruit and beans, at times planting the two species together so that the organ pipe cacti cast shade over the tepary beans. This practice shields the tepary beans from the most intense heat and light and, in turn, helps keep soil moisture from evaporating. Text 2: Tepary beans are well suited to desert conditions but flourish most when shaded. Taking a cue from O'odham farmers, who often deliberately grow tepary beans in the shade of sun-tolerant species such as organ pipe cacti to shield them from sun and heat, Gary Nabhan and colleagues planted tepary beans beneath solar panels in the Sonoran desert. The plants thrived, which suggested to the researchers that the panels offer a benefit much like the one organ pipe cacti provide.
option a: Compared with Nabhan's approach, the O'odham approach has the advantage of producing beans.
option b: Organ pipe cacti grow best when planted in shaded areas, while tepary beans do not require shade to thrive.
option c: Nabhan's team's method could be refined to more actively prevent soil moisture from evaporating.
option d: Organ pipe cacti can provide shade that protects tepary beans from high-intensity heat and light.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Both texts state that organ pipe cacti shade tepary beans from intense heat and light.

question: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the statement? Millions of Metric Tons of Copper Mined in 1995 and 2020. Country | 1995 | 2020. Zambia | 0.33 | 0.85. Peru | 0.38 | 2.15. Indonesia | 0.44 | 0.51. Canada | 0.73 | 0.59. While researching a paper on metal exports, a student comes across a table showing how much copper was mined in each of four countries during 1995 and 2020. The student notes that in 1995, Zambia mined ______
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The table lists Zambia's 1995 figure as 0.33 million metric tons.

question: Which choice most effectively uses data from the graph to complete the researcher's example? Graph titled "Days per Winter That Lakes Have Surface Ice," with a vertical axis showing Days (0, 40, 80, 120, 160, 200) and a horizontal axis showing two winters (1980-81 and 2005-06) for three lakes: Oulujärvi, Mirror Lake, and Lake Neusiedl. Freshwater lakes at or above 45° north latitude, such as Lake Mjøsa in Norway, commonly build up surface ice during winter. A study spanning 1980 to 2006 found that, on the whole, the number of days per winter that such lakes carry measurable surface ice is falling. A researcher argued, however, that certain lakes have instead experienced a longer duration of ice, offering as an example ______
option a: Lake Neusiedl, which had more days of ice in the winter of 2005-06 than it did in the winter of 1980-81.
option b: both Lake Neusiedl and Oulujärvi, which had fewer than 195 days of ice in the winter of 1980-81.
option c: both Lake Neusiedl and Oulujärvi, which had more than 105 days of ice in the winter of 2005-06.
option d: both Mirror Lake and Oulujärvi, which had more days of ice in the winter of 2005-06 than they did in the winter of 1980-81.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Only Lake Neusiedl shows more ice days in 2005-06 than in 1980-81, supporting the increase claim.

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? Aubergine is a 2016 play written by Julia Cho. ______ play had its first performance at the Playwrights Horizons theater in New York City.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The singular demonstrative 'This' correctly modifies the singular noun 'play.'

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? Okpik: Little Village in the Arctic is a short documentary that was released in 2022. It ______ directed by the Inuit filmmaker Tiffany Ayalik.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The singular subject 'It' requires the singular verb 'was.'

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? Although she is best known as a novelist—thanks largely to the success of her 2020 horror novel Mexican Gothic—Silvia Moreno-Garcia launched her career as a prolific writer of short stories. The list of more than 75 short ______ she published before Mexican Gothic includes pieces like "King of Sand and Stormy Seas" (2006) and "The Performance" (2012).
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The restrictive clause 'that she published' needs no punctuation before it.

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? To assess the biodiversity of the city's urban forest, a 2024 study catalogued every tree in Amsterdam. After finding that administrative unit GT23 had a 1.45 ratio of native to non-native trees, the researchers ______ efforts to preserve the biodiversity of the trees in that unit and in other areas with a similarly high ratio.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The main clause needs the finite past-tense verb 'recommended.'

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? Iain Stott works as a biologist at the University of ______ conducts research on plants.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: A period and 'He' correctly separate the two independent clauses.

question: The student wants to emphasize a similarity between Almaty and Auckland. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal? While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes: Typically, a country's capital is also its most populous city. In Kazakhstan, the capital is Nur-Sultan, while its largest city by population is Almaty. In New Zealand, the capital is Wellington, while its largest city by population is Auckland.
option a: The most populous city in Kazakhstan is Almaty, but its capital is Nur-Sultan.
option b: While Almaty is in Kazakhstan, Auckland is in New Zealand.
option c: Although neither is a capital city, both Almaty and Auckland are the most populous cities in their countries.
option d: The capital of Kazakhstan is Nur-Sultan; the capital of New Zealand is Wellington.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Only this choice highlights the shared trait: each is its country's largest city but not its capital.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase? The habit of sorting authors into separate literary movements often leads scholars to miss the finer points of an individual author's style. Someone studying the works of William Henry Furness, for example, might unintentionally ______ subtleties in his writing by attending only to the most obvious ways his style aligns with transcendentalism.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: 'Disregard' fits the idea of overlooking subtleties by focusing only on obvious traits.
